trust_decision.summary: A tenant with create/update on fission.io environments or functions decides which PodSpec/Container fields the fission-executor and fission-builder (both privileged, pod-creating SAs) copy into runtime, pool, build and container pods; the decision is made twice - at admission in pkg/webhook/environment.go (Environment.Validate) / pkg/webhook/function.go (Function.Validate) and again in pkg/executor/util/MergePodSpec, which overlays the stored spec onto the controller-built pod.

landing_point.why: The advisory names Environment PodSpec passthrough, so an engineer looks first at Environment.Validate/EnvironmentSpec.Validate (validation.go:392-422) and adds a podspec field check there; the real fix also has to land in the executor/buildermgr merge layer and the webhook verb registration.

fix_sites.entry_point: shared helper called from both admission webhooks (fix.diff:76)
fix_sites.module_kind: new validation helper in the API package

fix_sites.entry_point: controller reconcile of Environment/Function CRs: poolmgr and newdeploy deployment creation, buildermgr builder deployment, container executor function deployment
Environment validating webhook verb list (CREATE -> CREATE;UPDATE)
rendered ValidatingWebhookConfiguration operations for environments (adds UPDATE next to CREATE)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: MergePodSpec is a generic 'merge these two pod specs' plumbing utility in another package, also used for the operator's own podSpecPatch, so an engineer reading an Environment-CRD advisory treats it as a consumer of already-validated data rather than a security boundary.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Pod-level SecurityContext must keep flowing from the target spec: the chart ships runAsNonRoot/runAsUser=10001/runAsGroup=10001/fsGroup=10001 as operator hardening for runtime and builder pods, and benign capabilities such as NET_BIND_SERVICE/CHOWN and non-hostPath volumes (configMap/secret) must stay accepted, so a blanket reject-everything-securityContext fix breaks legitimate deployments.

O6_input_shapes: serviceAccountName plus the deprecated alias serviceAccount (DeprecatedServiceAccount)
volumes[] elements whose source is HostPath (array/slice shape, name reported in the error)
*bool fields privileged and allowPrivilegeEscalation inside containers[].securityContext
capabilities.add[] array matched against a deny-list (SYS_ADMIN, NET_ADMIN, SYS_PTRACE, SYS_MODULE, DAC_READ_SEARCH, DAC_OVERRIDE) with benign entries preserved
the same fields arriving as a merge target through MergePodSpec rather than as the CR's own podspec

O7_producer.where: pkg/executor/util/merge.go:58 (MergePodSpec builds the effective pod spec the sink receives; the admission check ValidatePodSpecSafety never calls it)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Environment.spec.runtime.container and spec.builder.container is a full apiv1.Container (privileged, allowPrivilegeEscalation, capabilities.add, image/command) merged into the runtime or builder container by MergeContainer with no podspec-safety check; when the sibling PodSpec is nil, MergePodSpec - and therefore the fix's sanitize - is never called at all.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Container is a separate, documented alternative field ('you can set either PodSpec or Container, but not both', pkg/apis/core/v1/types.go:572), and the new helper takes a *apiv1.PodSpec, so a solver argues the Container route is a different feature outside the advisory's podspec passthrough scope.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: 3 packages from the landing point (apis/core/v1 -> executor/executortype/{poolmgr,newdeploy} and buildermgr); the merge path only runs its sanitize when env.Spec.Runtime.PodSpec / env.Spec.Builder.PodSpec is non-nil

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a sanitize step on the MergeContainer path, mirroring sanitizeContainerSecurityContext on the MergePodSpec path
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the same privileged / allowPrivilegeEscalation / capabilities data arrives through env.Spec.Runtime.Container at MergeContainer one function above MergePodSpec, so a maintainer would plausibly write the helper there (and this is exactly the O8 gap).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: deny or strip ShareProcessNamespace from the merged pod
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: it is the same per-field propagation block as hostPID/hostIPC on the lines above; a tenant sharing the runtime pod's process namespace could ptrace the fetcher container that holds the projected SA token, so a maintainer extending the denylist would naturally add it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: drop ImagePullSecrets / HostAliases appended from the target spec
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: same append-style propagation as the neighbouring fields; hostAliases can redirect DNS for the fetcher container, so a maintainer hardening this block could extend the same denylist.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: reject a user container that reuses a fission system container name (fetcher/builder) inside Environment.Validate
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Environment.Validate already walks Runtime.PodSpec.Containers to enforce a container-name rule there, so adding one more container-level rejection in the same loop is the obvious place.

O9_family: CWE-269/CWE-284/CWE-693 - improper privilege management: container-sandbox escape via user-controlled PodSpec/Container fields passed through to pods scheduled by the privileged fission-executor and fission-builder service accounts

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add one ValidatePodSpecSafety-style denylist to EnvironmentSpec.Validate/FunctionSpec.Validate that rejects hostNetwork/hostPID/privileged in spec.runtime.podspec, leave the UPDATE verb, the merge layer and the Container route untouched, and verify only through the new validator.

out_of_scope_notes: A tenant container named 'fetcher' merges by name into the fetcher container (pkg/executor/util/merge.go:201-232) and can override its image/command before MountFetcherSATokenOnFetcher hands it the projected SA token; that is the already-published GHSA-85g2/8wcj property, not this advisory's, and was not pursued.

MessageQueueTrigger.spec.podspec already has its own allowlist protection from GHSA-7m8x (pkg/webhook/messagequeuetrigger.go:53-89, pkg/executor/util/merge_allowlist.go:47-110); it is a different mechanism and outside this advisory.
